title: What if every university became a country?
narrator: Deadpan documentary: calm and dry, treats the impossible premise like a serious report. The jokes land through understatement.
logline: Every campus becomes a nation. Stanford outsizes two real countries, and meal swipes become money.

cues.onScreen: What if every college became a country?
cues.narration: What if every college became a country?

cues.onScreen: Right now, colleges are just dots on a map.
cues.narration: Right now, colleges are dots on a map.

cues.onScreen: They already have colors, mascots, and loud fans.
cues.narration: But they already have flags, mascots, and fans who chant.
Then every campus declares independence. At the same time.

cues.onScreen: Borders pop up across the whole map.
cues.narration: Borders go up overnight. The UN has 193 members. It is about to need more chairs.

cues.onScreen: Stanford alone is bigger than Monaco and Vatican City.
cues.narration: Stanford alone: bigger than Monaco and Vatican City combined.

cues.onScreen: Problem 1: Visiting a friend needs a passport.
cues.narration: Border day: visiting your friend across the street now needs a passport.

cues.onScreen: Problem 2: Meal swipes become the currency.
cues.narration: Meal swipes become money. MIT pays in pizza. Stanford, in equity.

cues.onScreen: Problem 3: Football games turn into peace talks.
cues.narration: Summit day: two campuses dispute one parking lot. It goes to overtime.

cues.onScreen: So they all form one giant Student Union.
cues.narration: So they form one giant Student Union. Of nations.

cues.onScreen: What would your college's flag look like?

notes: Stanford is about 33.8 km² (v08.c.stanford_km2, verified). Monaco (about 2 km²) plus Vatican City (about 0.44 km²) is about 2.44 km², so 'bigger than both combined' holds by a wide margin once those two areas are verified.
